hypothesis: Concatenating feature representations from both Stage 3 (8x8 spatial resolution, 384 channels) and Stage 4 (4x4 spatial resolution, 768 channels) with feature standardization yields a 1152-dimensional multi-scale backbone output. This provides both the SSL projection head and the downstream linear probe with access to rich mid-level visual structures alongside high-level semantics, improving linear evaluation performance under Joint DCL + Barlow Twins pretraining.
rationale: In previous runs, deepening Stage 3 alone (Iter 14) or altering the projection head structure (Iter 19) degraded performance or caused bottlenecking. On 32x32 images, standard pooling at Stage 4 (4x4 feature map) discards fine-grained mid-level spatial details present at Stage 3 (8x8 feature map). Fusing global average pooled features from both Stage 3 and Stage 4 (with BatchNorm standardization) preserves multi-scale visual hierarchies, boosting linear probe discriminability without adding overhead.
expected_effect: Increases linear probe validation top-1 accuracy beyond the current best of 0.6200 by providing multi-scale representation capacity to the evaluator while maintaining the optimal DCL + Barlow Twins pretraining objective.
change_summary:
1. Modified CIFARResNet26AntiAliased backbone to extract and pool features from both Stage 3 (384-dim) and Stage 4 (768-dim), concatenating and standardizing them via BatchNorm1d to produce a 1152-dim multi-scale feature vector (backbone_dim=1152).
2. Adjusted ProjectionHead input dimension from 768 to 1152 (1152 -> 4096 -> 4096 -> 2048).
3. Retained the best-performing Joint DCL + Barlow Twins Feature Decorrelation loss (tau=0.10, bt_weight=0.5, lambda_param=5e-3) and detail-preserving CIFAR-100 augmentations from Iter 16.
